claims.title: Exact partition refinement returns the coarsest hidden-law bisimulation
claims.scope: finite rational hidden Markov source-law models with action-independent transitions and observation channels
assumptions: states in one candidate block must have identical categorical source laws and observation-channel rows
transition behavior is compared by exact probability mass assigned to every current partition block
finite refinement continues until a stable partition is reached
nonclaims: behavioral equivalence is not metaphysical or physical identity
finite exact refinement is not a complexity guarantee for very large models

claims.title: The hidden-law bisimulation quotient preserves the finite observable class process
claims.scope: the quotient model induced by the coarsest exact hidden-law bisimulation
assumptions: quotient initial mass is aggregated over final equivalence blocks
quotient transition probability is the representative-independent probability mass into each final block
source laws and observation rows are constant within each final block
nonclaims: the quotient does not preserve unmodeled observables that reveal internal state identity
quotient-state count is not parent-substrate memory

claims.title: Hidden-law bisimulation preserves all declared finite-horizon Bayesian coding values
claims.scope: no-signal, noisy-observation, perfect-current-state, and expected clairvoyant zero-error prefix-coding values under one finite horizon and rational switching charge
assumptions: the original and quotient models use the same confusion graph and codebook action family
all codebook stage costs depend on hidden state only through its categorical source law
hidden transitions and observation channels are action independent
nonclaims: value preservation need not hold after adding an action or observation that exposes internal state identity
the theorem is finite horizon rather than an unqualified infinite-horizon claim

claims.title: Syntactic hidden-state duplication does not imply predictive-state multiplicity
claims.scope: finite hidden-state refinements that preserve source laws, observation rows, and transition mass into every behavioral equivalence class
assumptions: duplicated states are merged by the exact hidden-law bisimulation relation
the predictive interface is restricted to the declared source observations, signals, codebook costs, and hidden dynamics
nonclaims: the theorem does not deny that internal labels may matter under a richer interface
syntactic multiplicity is not converted into observer multiplicity or simulation evidence

claims.title: Three-state internal-transition model quotients exactly to two predictive hidden states
claims.scope: the declared three-state rational example with states zero and one sharing source/signal labels and equal transition mass into blocks {0,1} and {2}
assumptions: the source laws, observation rows, initial belief, and transition rows are exactly those exercised by the bounded test
the coding horizon and switch charge are supplied to the quotient-value checker
nonclaims: the numerical quotient transition matrix is instance specific
the example is not a claim about real-world hidden-state ontology

claims.title: Bounded exact hidden-law refinement and quotient-value audit
claims.scope: the finite rational hidden-state partitions, quotient models, paths, beliefs, and coding values exercised by the repository tests
assumptions: all configured path, candidate, partition, and prefix-shape caps complete without truncation
Python Fraction arithmetic is used for every finite transition, belief, and cost calculation
nonclaims: bounded test completion is not a scalability theorem
finite quotient agreement is not evidence that reality is simulated
